Here's where the little project stands this afternoon. We have a working first version, a short list of changes, and enough notes to explain why we chose the simpler route. The button now uses the same label in both menus, and the drawer opens without catching on the cable. I kept the older copy because comparing the two makes the improvement easier to understand. There is still one awkward corner near the window, but it can wait until we have finished the parts people use every day. The next pass will focus on clear names, useful messages, and an easy way to undo a mistaken choice. Nobody needs to remember the whole arrangement at once. A good starting point is enough, and the rest can become familiar through use. I would rather take a little extra time now than leave someone guessing later. When we stop for the evening, the notes will say what works, what needs another look, and where to begin tomorrow. That should make coming back feel comfortable instead of confusing.
